mainTopic: What the word הכל ('everyone') comes to include in a long series of rulings, from מגילה and זימון to טומאה, פרה אדומה, שחיטה and moving to ארץ ישראל
overview: The גמרא goes through a long list of rulings that begin with the word הכל ('everyone'). For each one it asks לאתויי מאי: whom does 'everyone' come to include? Reading the מגילה includes women, and being obligated in זימון includes women and slaves. Being counted toward a זימון includes a קטן who knows to Whom we bless. For זיבה, even a one-day-old baby becomes impure; רבי יהודה learns this from 'איש איש', and רבי ישמעאל learns it from 'לזכר ולנקבה', holding that דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם. For טמא מת and נגעים a child is included, and the גמרא explains what the word איש teaches in each case: no כרת for a child, and only a man tears his clothes and grows his hair. It goes on to inspecting נגעים, mixing and sprinkling the פרה אדומה water, and שחיטה. The amud ends by asking what הכל adds in the rule about moving to ארץ ישראל, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading the מגילה includes women
steps.stepSummary: The word הכל in 'everyone is obligated to read the מגילה' comes to include women, following רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Everyone is obligated to read the מגילה — this comes to include] what? It includes women. This follows רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said that women are obligated to read the מגילה, because they too were part of that miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes asking what 'everyone' adds about reading the מגילה, and answers that it adds women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think women are exempt, since many time-bound מצוות do not obligate women. The word הכל teaches that they are included. The reason, from רבי יהושע בן לוי, is that women were also saved in the פורים miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in an extra case
The מצוה of reading מגילת אסתר on פורים
They too were part of that miracle, the reason women are obligated

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard source for the הלכה that women are obligated in reading the מגילה.

phrases.english: what?
phrases.notes: This finishes the question from just before: 'Everyone is obligated to read the מגילה' — who does that come to include?

phrases.english: To include women,
and this is in line with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Women are obligated in reading the Megillah,
for they too were in that miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the לאתויי מאי question about מקרא מגילה that was asked just before this point.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל adds women, who are obligated because they also were part of the miracle.
steps.whatToRemember: Women are obligated in מקרא מגילה because אף הן היו באותו הנס.

steps.title: What does 'everyone is obligated in זימון' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ruling 'everyone is obligated in זימון' and asks what the word הכל adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in זימון' — what does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next ruling in the list and sets up its question. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זימון is the group invitation to say ברכת המזון together. The question is the same pattern as before: who would we have thought is left out, so that the word 'everyone' is needed to include them?

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, the key word the גמרא is analyzing
Are obligated
The group call to bless together before ברכת המזון

phrases.english: 'Everyone is obligated in zimmun' —
to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same לאתויי מאי question to a new הכל ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which group the word הכל adds to the obligation of זימון.

steps.title: Women and slaves can form their own זימון
steps.stepSummary: The word הכל adds women and slaves, based on a ברייתא that says each group forms a זימון by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes women and slaves. As a ברייתא teaches: women form a זימון for themselves, and slaves form a זימון for themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everyone' comes to include women and slaves, and backs this up with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that women and slaves are part of the זימון system. Each group can do its own זימון when they eat together as a group of their own kind. That is why the ruling says 'everyone.'

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves (here meaning non-Jewish slaves owned by Jews, who keep some מצוות)
They form a זימון among themselves

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says each group does זימון 'for themselves.' It does not say women and slaves join together with each other in one זימון.

phrases.english: To include women and slaves,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Women form a zimmun for themselves,
and slaves form a zimmun for themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women and slaves, each of whom form a זימון among themselves.

steps.title: What does 'everyone joins a זימון' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ruling 'everyone is counted toward a זימון' and asks what it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone joins together for a זימון' — what does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question about who can be counted to make up the group needed for a זימון. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling is different from the last one. The last one was about who is obligated to do זימון. This one is about who can be counted to complete the group.

keyTerms.meaning: Join together, are counted to complete the required number

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 2. 'Obligated in זימון' and 'counted toward a זימון' are two separate rulings, and each one adds a different group.

phrases.english: 'Everyone joins together for zimmun' —
to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related but separate ruling about זימון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the word הכל adds to those who can be counted for a זימון.

steps.title: A child who knows to Whom we bless is counted
steps.stepSummary: The word הכל adds a קטן who understands to Whom we bless, following רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes a קטן who knows to Whom we bless. As רב נחמן said: one who knows to Whom we bless can be counted for a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everyone' includes a child who understands that our ברכות are said to ה׳, and it brings רב נחמן as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is not normally obligated in מצוות. Still, if he understands Whom the ברכה is addressed to, he can complete the group for a זימון. The test is his understanding, not his age.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child under בר מצוה
Knows to Whom we bless, meaning he understands that the ברכה is to ה׳
We form a זימון counting him

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard for when a child can be counted toward a זימון.

phrases.english: To include a minor
who knows to Whom we bless,
as Rav Naḥman said:
One who knows to Whom we bless —
we may form a zimmun with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קטן who knows to Whom we bless is counted for a זימון.

steps.title: What does 'everyone becomes impure through זיבה' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ruling 'everyone becomes impure through זיבה' and asks what the word הכל adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone becomes impure through זיבה' — what does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from ברכות to the laws of טומאה, asking the same question about a ruling on זיבה. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זיבה is a type of bodily discharge that makes a man impure as a זב. The question is which person we might have thought could not become a זב, so that the word 'everyone' is needed to include him.

keyTerms.meaning: Become impure
An abnormal discharge that makes a man impure as a זב

phrases.english: 'Everyone becomes impure through ziva' —
phrases.notes: משנה זבים 2:1

phrases.english: to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same pattern to a new area, the laws of טומאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the word הכל adds to those who can become impure through זיבה.

steps.title: Even a one-day-old baby can become a זב
steps.stepSummary: The word הכל adds a one-day-old baby, learned from the doubled words 'איש איש' in the פסוק, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes a baby one day old. As a ברייתא teaches: the פסוק could have said 'a man.' Why does it say 'any man' (איש איש)? To include a one-day-old baby, who becomes impure through זיבה. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'everyone' includes even a newborn baby, and it brings a ברייתא that learns this from the extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'איש איש' instead of just 'איש.' The extra word is read as adding someone who is not yet a grown man, even a baby one day old. The ברייתא tells us this is the opinion of רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby on the day of his birth, one day old
'Any man' (literally 'a man, a man'), a doubled word that the ברייתא reads as including more cases
Why does the פסוק say this? A formula pointing to an extra word
To include

steps.whatToRemember: Each הכל in this list adds one specific group: women for the מגילה, women and slaves for being obligated in זימון, a child who understands the ברכה for being counted in a זימון, and a day-old baby for זיבה.

phrases.english: To include a day-old baby,
as it is taught in a baraita:
'A man' would be enough; why does the verse say 'any man'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:2

phrases.english: To include a baby one day old
who becomes impure through ziva,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק closely.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A one-day-old baby becomes impure through זיבה, learned from איש איש, according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Another source: 'male or female' includes young and old
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says the extra 'איש' is not needed, because 'לזכר ולנקבה' already includes every male and female, young or old.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: You don't need that. The פסוק says 'and the זב, whether male or female.' 'Male' means any male, young or old. 'Female' means any female, young or old.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different source for the rule that even a baby becomes a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learned the baby from the doubled 'איש איש'. רבי ישמעאל says the words 'לזכר ולנקבה' already cover everyone, of any age. The ruling is the same; only the source changes.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. The earlier source is unnecessary.
A person who becomes impure through a certain bodily discharge
Male
Female

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
It is not necessary,
phrases.notes: He means there's no need to learn the baby from the doubled 'איש איש' in step 7.

phrases.english: for the verse says:
"And of the one who has an issue, whether male or female"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:33

phrases.english: "Male": anyone who is male,
whether a child or an adult;
"Female": anyone who is female,
whether a child or an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same rule taught in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'לזכר ולנקבה' include males and females of every age, babies too

steps.title: Then why does the Torah double 'man, man'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'male or female' already covers everyone, the doubled 'איש איש' seems to have no job.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'איש איש'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל asks a question on his own approach. If the baby is learned from 'לזכר ולנקבה', what is the doubled word for? This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual way of learning פסוקים expects every extra word to teach something. Since רבי ישמעאל no longer uses 'איש איש' for the baby, he has to explain why it is written.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. If what was just said is true.
Why does the פסוק need to say this? What does it come to teach?

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "any man" (literally, "a man, a man")?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the leftover doubled word in רבי ישמעאל's own approach
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the doubled 'איש איש' teaches if it is not the source for the baby

steps.title: The Torah speaks the way people speak
steps.stepSummary: The doubled 'איש איש' is just normal human speech. No new law is learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spoke in the way people normally talk.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers that the double word is only a normal way of talking, so it does not teach anything extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the famous rule דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם. רבי ישמעאל holds that a repeated word can simply be ordinary style. That is the real disagreement with רבי יהודה, who learns a law from the repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah spoke in human language. Not every extra or doubled word teaches a law.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and רבי ישמעאל agree that a baby becomes a זב. They argue only about the source: 'איש איש' versus 'לזכר ולנקבה', because רבי ישמעאל holds דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.
steps.whyThisMatters: דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם is a well-known rule of how to learn פסוקים, and it comes up across ש״ס.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled word is ordinary human speech and teaches no law

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for impurity from a dead body?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'everyone becomes impure through טמא מת' and asks what the word הכל adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone becomes impure through the impurity of a dead body.' What does this come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next 'הכל' ruling, about טומאת מת, and asks who the word 'everyone' is meant to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same pattern as before. Each 'הכל' should include someone we might have left out. Here the גמרא wants to know who that is for impurity from a dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity that comes from a dead body
To add what? Who is being included?

phrases.english: "Everyone becomes impure through impurity of a corpse":
what does this come to add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'הכל' rulings with a new case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom the word הכל includes for impurity from a dead body

steps.title: It adds a child, learned from 'the people who were there'
steps.stepSummary: הכל adds a קטן. You might think 'איש' leaves out children, so the פסוק 'ועל הנפשות' teaches that everyone present becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It adds a child. You might have thought: the פסוק says 'a man who becomes impure and does not purify himself.' A man, yes; a child, no. So it teaches us: 'and on the people who were there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הכל includes a child. It explains why we might have thought otherwise, and which פסוק shows that a child is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'איש' could make us think only adults become impure from a dead body. But the פסוק about sprinkling the purifying water says 'the people who were there', with no age limit. So a child becomes impure too.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child
You might have thought. This sets up a mistaken first idea.
So it teaches us. This brings the correct idea.
Purify himself (here, from impurity from a dead body)

phrases.english: To add a minor;
it might enter your mind to say:
"A man who becomes impure and does not purify himself":
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:20

phrases.english: a "man", yes; a minor, no.
So it teaches us:
"And upon the persons who were there."
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:18. 'The persons' sets no age limit, so a child who was there is impure too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל adds a קטן, based on 'ועל הנפשות אשר היו שם'

steps.title: Then what does the word 'man' leave out?
steps.stepSummary: If a child also becomes impure, what is the word 'איש' in the פסוק meant to exclude?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does 'man' come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If a child becomes impure, the word 'איש' seems to have no job, so what does it exclude?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just said 'איש' does not exclude a child from becoming impure. Still, the word is written, so it should teach something. The גמרא asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: But then... This introduces a challenge.
To exclude what? Who is being left out?

phrases.english: But then, what does "man" come to exclude?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leftover word 'איש' after step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a child becomes impure, the word 'איש' seems to teach nothing

steps.title: 'Man' exempts a child from כרת
steps.stepSummary: The word 'איש' teaches that a child is not punished with כרת. It does not teach that a child stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude a child from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'איש' leaves a child out of the כרת punishment that the same פסוק mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says the person who stays impure is cut off with כרת. 'איש' limits that punishment to adults. The impurity itself still applies to a child.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two laws. A child does become impure from a dead body. He is only free from the כרת punishment.

phrases.english: To exclude a minor from karet.
phrases.notes: כרת is mentioned in that same פסוק, במדבר 19:20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איש' seems to exclude a child from becoming impure
steps.terutzMaskana: 'איש' excludes a child only from כרת. He still becomes impure.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for נגעים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'everyone becomes impure through נגעים' and asks what הכל adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone becomes impure through נגעים.' What does this come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next 'הכל' ruling, about impurity from נגעים, and asks who it includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is the same pattern again: each 'הכל' should include someone we might otherwise leave out.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin marks (צרעת) that make a person impure

phrases.english: "Everyone becomes impure through leprous marks":
what does this come to add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case in the 'הכל' series
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom the word הכל includes for נגעים

steps.title: It adds a child, even though the פסוק says 'man'
steps.stepSummary: הכל adds a קטן. You might think 'איש צרוע' leaves out children, so the word הכל teaches that they are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It adds a child. You might have thought: it is written 'a man with צרעת.' A man, yes; a child, no. So it teaches us that a child is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הכל includes a child for נגעים, even though the פסוק uses the word 'איש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's word 'איש צרוע' could suggest that only adults become impure from נגעים. Here the word 'everyone' itself teaches that a child becomes impure too.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת

steps.whatToRemember: In both טמא מת and נגעים, הכל comes to include a קטן, even though the פסוקים use the word 'איש'.

phrases.english: To add a minor.
It might enter your mind to say:
"A leprous man" is written,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:44

phrases.english: so a man, yes; a minor, no.
So it teaches us.
phrases.notes: No new פסוק is brought here. The word 'everyone' itself is what teaches that a child is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל adds a קטן, who also becomes impure through נגעים

steps.title: Maybe a child really is not made impure by נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer: maybe a קטן truly is not made impure through נגעים, just as the word איש suggests.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 16. Maybe a קטן really is left out of טומאת נגעים, so there is nothing for הכל to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said that without הכל we might think a child is left out because the פסוק says 'איש צרוע'. Now the גמרא asks: why not actually rule that way? This sets up the need to find a פסוק that clearly includes a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so — maybe the 'mistaken' idea is actually the הלכה
A minor, a child
The impurity caused by skin afflictions (צרעת)

phrases.english: But say that it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe a child really doesn't become impure through נגעים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 16 by suggesting the excluded case should stay excluded.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 16 that a קטן is made impure by נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word איש in the פסוק seems to leave out a child, so maybe that is the real הלכה and הכל adds nothing.

steps.title: The word אדם includes everyone
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אדם כי יהיה בעור בשרו' uses the general word אדם, which includes every person, child or adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'אדם, when there shall be in the skin of his flesh' — meaning any person at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a קטן must be impure, because the opening פסוק of נגעים says אדם, which covers anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איש can sound like 'grown man', but אדם is a general word for any human being. Since the main פסוק about נגעים uses אדם, a child is clearly included, and we cannot simply rule that a קטן stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A person — a general word that includes anyone
In any case, no matter what
In the skin of his flesh — where the נגע appears

phrases.english: 'A person, when there shall be in the skin of his flesh,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2

phrases.english: in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם כִּי יִהְיֶה בְעוֹר בְּשָׂרוֹ מִכָּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק with a general word that includes a child.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a קטן is not made impure by נגעים because the פסוק says איש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word אדם includes everyone, so a קטן is made impure.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say איש
steps.stepSummary: If אדם already includes everyone, the word איש in 'איש צרוע הוא' seems to have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'איש'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if everyone is included through אדם, what is the word איש teaching?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word in the תורה teaches something. Once אדם covers everyone, איש cannot be there to include people. It must be teaching something else, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? — asking what a word is for
A man

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'man'?
phrases.notes: From the words 'איש צרוע הוא' in ויקרא 13:44.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 18: if אדם includes everyone, the word איש looks extra.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אדם already includes all people, איש seems to add nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the word צרוע adds a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. איש alone would mean only a man, but the extra word 'והצרוע' in the next פסוק adds a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'Man' — I only know about a man. From where do I know about a woman? When it says 'and the צרוע', there are two here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering with a ברייתא. First the ברייתא shows that a woman is also impure through נגעים, from the word 'והצרוע'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that from איש we would only know about a man. But the next פסוק repeats 'the צרוע' even though we already know who it is talking about, so the extra word adds a second person — a woman. This sets up the question of what איש is really for, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: For what was taught in a ברייתא
From where do we know?
A person with צרעת
Here there are two — the extra word includes another person

phrases.english: For that which is taught: 'Man' —
I only have a man;
from where do I know a woman?
When it says 'and the צרוע' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:45

phrases.english: there are two here.
phrases.notes: The פסוק didn't need to say 'the צרוע' again, so the extra mention adds a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְתַנְיָא אִישׁ אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אִישׁ אִשָּׁה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering Step 19 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a ברייתא that explains the words איש and צרוע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איש seems to be an extra word with no job.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא shows women are included through 'והצרוע', setting up the real job of איש.

steps.title: איש teaches that only a man tears his clothes and grows his hair
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes: איש refers to the rules in the next פסוק — a man with צרעת lets his hair grow and tears his clothes, but a woman does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'man'? For the matter below: a man lets his hair grow and tears his clothes, but a woman does not let her hair grow and does not tear her clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the answer: the word איש is not about who becomes impure, but about who must tear clothes and let hair grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since women are already included in טומאה, איש must teach a different detail. It points to the mourning-like rules of the צרוע in the next פסוק and limits them to a man. So איש does not leave anyone out of טומאה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the פסוק come to teach?
Lets his hair grow wild
Tears his clothes
For the matter written below (in the next פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The word איש by נגעים does not leave out women or children from טומאה. Everyone is impure; איש only teaches that a man, not a woman, tears his clothes and lets his hair grow.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two questions: who becomes impure (everyone) and who tears clothes and grows hair (only a man). איש answers only the second one.

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'man'?
For the matter below —
phrases.notes: Pointing to ויקרא 13:45, about torn clothes and loose hair.

phrases.english: a man lets his hair grow and tears his clothes,
but a woman does not let her hair grow and does not tear her clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 20 and gives the final answer to Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word איש a different job: limiting the rules of tearing and hair-growing to men.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איש seems to have no purpose once everyone is included in טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: איש teaches that only a man with צרעת tears his clothes and lets his hair grow.

steps.title: What does 'everyone may inspect נגעים' add
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two statements that everyone may inspect נגעים and asks what the word הכל comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone may inspect נגעים', 'Everyone is fit to inspect נגעים' — what does this come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new הכל statement, this time about who may look at נגעים, and asks what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier steps: the גמרא sees the word הכל and assumes it includes someone we might have left out. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Inspect the skin afflictions to decide if they are pure or impure
Fit, allowed
To add what? — what case does this word include?

phrases.english: 'Everyone may inspect leprous marks,'
'Everyone is fit to inspect leprous marks' —
to add what?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל רוֹאִין אֶת הַנְּגָעִים הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לִרְאוֹת אֶת הַנְּגָעִים לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new הכל statement, following the same pattern as Steps 15-16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is included by the word הכל in the rule about inspecting נגעים.

steps.title: הכל includes someone who is not an expert in נגעים
steps.stepSummary: הכל adds a person who is not an expert in the types of נגעים and their names.
steps.simpleTranslation: To add one who is not expert in them and in their names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הכל includes even someone who does not know the different kinds of נגעים or what they are called.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought only an expert who knows all the types and names of נגעים may inspect them. The word הכל teaches that even someone without that expertise is fit to inspect.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert, someone well-versed
Their names — the names of the different types of נגעים

phrases.english: To add one who is not expert
in them and in their names.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the different kinds of נגעים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הכל includes someone who is not an expert in the types of נגעים and their names.

steps.title: But a non-expert may not inspect נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer with a statement that a כהן who is not expert in the נגעים and their names may not inspect them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Master said: one who is not expert in them and their names may not inspect the נגעים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It quotes a teaching that a non-expert is not allowed to inspect נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said the word הכל includes a person who is not an expert in the types of נגעים and their names. Now a different statement says that exactly this kind of person may NOT inspect them. The two teachings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Inspects the marks of צרעת to rule on them

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
one who is not expert in them and in their names
does not inspect the נגעים!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that הכל includes a non-expert in נגעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching says outright that a non-expert may not inspect נגעים, which contradicts step 23.

steps.title: Two kinds of non-experts
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the two teachings speak about different people: one who understands when it is explained, and one who does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is not difficult. This teaching is about one who understands when they explain it to him. That teaching is about one who does not understand even when they explain it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the contradiction. He splits non-experts into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-expert who understands once someone explains it may inspect, and he is the one הכל includes. A non-expert who still does not understand after it is explained may not inspect. Now both teachings are true, each about a different person.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. The two sources talk about different cases
They explain it to him
He understands

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who is not an expert may still inspect נגעים, as long as he understands when someone explains it to him.

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is not difficult;
this is where they explain to him and he understands,
that is where they explain to him and he does not understand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one teaching for each kind of person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both teachings seemed to be about the same non-expert
steps.terutzMaskana: One who understands after an explanation is fit. One who does not understand even then is unfit.

steps.title: What does 'everyone may mix the ashes' include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word הכל adds in the משנה that everyone is fit to mix the ashes of the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Everyone is fit to sanctify." What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה that uses the word הכל. It asks who that word comes to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as before: a משנה says 'everyone', so the גמרא looks for a person we might have thought was excluded. Here the topic is preparing the water with the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

keyTerms.meaning: To 'sanctify', meaning to put the ashes of the פרה אדומה into the water
What does it come to include?
Fit, qualified

phrases.english: "Everyone is fit to sanctify" —
phrases.notes: This means mixing the ashes of the פרה אדומה with the water.

phrases.english: to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next הכל statement in the series that began in step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the word הכל adds in the case of mixing the ashes

steps.title: A minor or a woman, depending on the opinion
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, הכל adds a קטן. According to the רבנן, it adds an אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה it comes to include a minor, and according to the רבנן it comes to include a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that it depends on whose opinion we follow. Each opinion has a different person that הכל adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows a קטן, so for him הכל adds the קטן. The רבנן do not allow a קטן but do allow a woman, so for them הכל adds the אשה. The next step brings the משנה where these opinions appear.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child under the age of מצוות
A woman

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, to include a minor,
and according to the Rabbis, to include a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יהודה, a קטן. For the רבנן, an אשה.

steps.title: The משנה that shows both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: everyone may mix the ashes except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן but disqualifies a woman and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Everyone is fit to sanctify, except a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor. רבי יהודה allows a minor, and disqualifies a woman and an androgynous person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the answer in step 27. It shows where each opinion is written in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא excludes only a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן, so a woman must be included, and that is what הכל adds for him. רבי יהודה allows a קטן but excludes a woman, so for him הכל can only be adding the קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute
A person who is mentally incompetent
Rules as fit
Rules as unfit
A person with both male and female features

steps.confusionAlert: The woman is not mentioned as allowed in the רבנן's list. We know she is fit for them only because she is not in the list of people they exclude.

phrases.english: As we learned: Everyone is fit to sanctify,
except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor;
Rabbi Yehuda deems a minor fit,
and deems a woman and a hermaphrodite unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 27
steps.raayaObject: That for the רבנן הכל adds a woman, and for רבי יהודה it adds a minor

steps.title: What does 'everyone may sprinkle' include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what הכל adds in the משנה that everyone is fit to sprinkle the purifying water.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Everyone is fit to sprinkle." What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another משנה with the word הכל, this time about sprinkling. It asks who is being added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling is the next stage after the water is prepared. It is put on a person who became טמא from a dead body. The גמרא again looks for the surprising person that 'everyone' includes.

keyTerms.meaning: To sprinkle the purifying water on someone who is טמא from a dead body

phrases.english: "Everyone is fit to sprinkle" —
to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next הכל statement in the series
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the word הכל adds in the case of sprinkling

steps.title: It includes an uncircumcised man
steps.stepSummary: הכל adds an ערל, following רבי אלעזר, who rules that an ערל's sprinkling is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include an uncircumcised man, following רבי אלעזר, for רבי אלעזר said: An uncircumcised man who sprinkled, his sprinkling is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הכל adds an ערל. It supports this with a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought an ערל cannot do this, since he is unfit for many holy things. רבי אלעזר rules that his sprinkling still works, and the משנה's הכל follows that view.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who is not circumcised
The act of sprinkling

phrases.english: To include an uncircumcised man,
and in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, as Rabbi Elazar said:
An uncircumcised man who sprinkled — his sprinkling is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ערל, whose sprinkling is valid according to רבי אלעזר

steps.title: What does 'everyone may slaughter' include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what הכל adds in the משנה that everyone may slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Everyone slaughters." What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה about שחיטה. It asks who the word הכל comes to add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the next example in the list of הכל statements. The answer in the next step will explain two additions, because this phrase appears twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter (an animal in the kosher way)

phrases.english: "Everyone slaughters" —
to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next הכל statement in the series
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the word הכל adds in the case of שחיטה

steps.title: A כותי and an apostate Jew
steps.stepSummary: The phrase הכל שוחטין appears twice. One time adds a כותי, and the other adds an ישראל משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: One comes to include a כותי, and one comes to include an apostate Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two additions, one for each time the phrase is said. Their שחיטה is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'everyone slaughters' is said twice, each time must teach something. One adds a כותי, and the other adds a Jew who has turned away from the תורה. Both might have been thought unfit to slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan
A Jew who has abandoned תורה observance
One (here, one of the two times the phrase appears)

steps.whatToRemember: The same pattern keeps repeating: whenever a משנה says הכל, it is adding someone we might have thought was excluded.

phrases.english: One to include a Samaritan,
phrases.notes: The words 'everyone slaughters' show up twice in the משניות, so each one adds someone.

phrases.english: and one to include an apostate Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One mention adds a כותי, and the other adds an ישראל משומד

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add in the rule about moving to the Land of Israel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word הכל comes to include in the משנה that says everyone can force others to move up to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Everyone can force others to go up to ארץ ישראל.' What does the word 'everyone' come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its list of משניות that start with הכל, and now asks what הכל adds in the rule about moving to ארץ ישראל. This line only sets up the question; the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in כתובות teaches that a family member can force the rest of the household to move to ארץ ישראל. The גמרא assumes the extra word הכל must be including someone you would not have expected. It now asks who that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Force others to go up, meaning to move to ארץ ישראל
The Land of Israel
What does it come to include?

steps.confusionAlert: מעלין here does not mean bringing a קרבן up on the מזבח. It means forcing family members to move up to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: 'Everyone can force others to go up to the Land of Israel'
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a משנה in כתובות (110b). It means a person can make his household move with him to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: What does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as steps 29 and 31, asking what הכל adds in yet another משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra person or case is included by the word הכל in the משנה about forcing a move to ארץ ישראל.
